subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps - Acme Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T15:02:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Hi Emma,

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please reply with any edits.

Summary of customer goals / pain points
- Latency: need consistent low-latency inference for patient-facing flows (p95 target ~100ms for ~256-token responses).
- Data isolation & compliance: production data must be isolated (VPC + dedicated GPUs), SOC 2 evidence required, audit logs retained >= 12 months.
- Scaling & cost predictability: want reserved capacity for steady traffic with the ability to handle bursts on demand.

Proposed Dedicated configuration (initial recommend):
- Reserved pool: 4x A100 GPUs (private pool, US-East region)
- Isolation: dedicated VPC + customer-managed KMS for keys
- Autoscale: baseline reserved throughput, burst to 8 GPUs for scheduled peaks (billing on burst usage)
- SLA: target 99.9% uptime; support for higher SLA (99.95%) as an add-on
- Observability: per-route latency + token-level cost breakdown + audit logs exported to your SIEM

Open questions for your team
1) Expected steady-state QPS and peak QPS (helps finalize GPU count).
2) Do you require separate pools for prod vs. staging (we can reserve per-environment or use isolation within the same pool)?
3) Any procurement/legal timelines we should be aware of?

Next steps (proposed)
- I will share an initial SOW + architecture diagram (attached).
- Schedule a technical workshop w/ your infra team and our Dev (Dev Patel) to confirm network and KMS details, are you available this week or next?
- I'll create a HubSpot deal record and route the SOW to your procurement/legal once we align on scope.

Attachments: Acme_Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_v1.pdf, redwood-dedicated-architecture.png

Thanks, looking forward to moving this forward.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0124

From: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acmehealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Rajiv Singh <rajiv.singh@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2027-05-08T17:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the detailed recap, this looks good. A few clarifications / firm requirements from our side:

Confirmed requirements
- Latency: yes — we need p95 <= 100ms for 256-token gen. If that requires a higher tier or additional optimization, flag it.
- Isolation: we do require logical separation between prod and staging. Ideally separate reserved pools for prod and staging (prod > staging in capacity), but if there's a recommended pattern that meets compliance we're open.
- GPUs: our initial expectation was 3 reserved A100s for prod and 1 for staging, with burst to 6 total across both pools. If your recommendation is 4 prod + burst to 8 for predictability, include the cost delta in the SOW.
- SLA: we need 99.95% for prod endpoints (this is a hard ask for our uptime guarantees).
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II evidence is required; logging/audit retention minimum 13 months (noted).

Other notes
- Region: must be US-East.
- Performance: assume typical request size ~180 tokens input, 256 tokens output during peak; measure on your standard benchmark and include expected p50/p95 numbers in the proposal.

Procurement timeline
- We're targeting a procurement decision by end of May. Legal may request minor redlines to liability/SLA clauses.

Ask: Please update the SOW with two SKU options (3xA100 prod + 1xA100 staging vs. 4xA100 prod + staging shared), explicit SLA pricing for 99.9% vs 99.95%, and the SOC 2 evidence packaging.

Thanks — Rajiv and I can do a quick tech check on Friday if that helps.

Emma
Emma Johnson
VP of Engineering, Acme Health
emma.johnson@acmehealth.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
To: Emma Johnson <emma.johnson@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.inference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: Dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Hi Emma, thanks for the quick turn. Appreciate the clear asks; we'll incorporate all of this. Short answers and next steps below.

Answers / adjustments
- GPUs & isolation: will include two SKUs in the SOW as requested: (A) Prod: 3xA100 reserved + Staging: 1xA100 reserved (burst to 6 total), and (B) Prod: 4xA100 reserved with shared staging capacity (burst to 8). We'll include a clear cost delta for each.
- SLA: we can offer 99.95% for prod as a paid SLA add-on — I'll include pricing and liability language in the SOW.
- SOC 2 / logs: we will bundle SOC 2 evidence + audit log export instructions; retention configured to 13 months per your requirement.
- Performance: Dev will run a 256-token p95 benchmark on the recommended config and add results to the tech appendix.

Proposed timeline
- Today: I'll send an updated SOW and an updated architecture diagram (see attached v2).
- Tomorrow: Dev (Dev Patel) will run a performance smoke test and share p50/p95 numbers.
- By 2027-05-12: Send final SOW for procurement/legal review and create DocuSign envelope.
- Mobility: If procurement needs faster turnaround, we can parallelize legal and tech workshop.

Requested next actions from Acme
1) Confirm whether Friday (2027-05-14) 11:00AM ET works for a 45-min technical workshop with Dev and Ben.
2) Share an estimated steady QPS and peak QPS (if you have telemetry) — we'll use this to validate SKU sizing.

Attachments: Acme_Dedicated_Capacity_SOW_v1.pdf (updated v2 attached), redwood-dedicated-architecture.png

I'll also push the HubSpot deal and include the DocuSign link once legal has the SOW.

Best,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
